_comment: Template for a real competition config. Fill the addresses the organiser gives you, set the account passwords in the environment variables named below, then run: node packages/gateway/dist/setup.js --template deploy/competition.example.json --out config/gateway.json. No password is written to this file.

checker.note: the grader. One or many entries; this only labels traffic in data/checker and the 'Чекер' tab. An unlisted checker stays safe regardless, because only known team subnets are policed

_ingress_ports: Port-redirection mode for a real network: clients keep dialling the service's own address, netfilter REDIRECTs the public port onto public+redirect_offset where the gateway listens, and the gateway forwards back to the same port on 127.0.0.1. Nothing in service or client config changes. Run deploy/iptables-forward.sh apply after configuring.
_protected_ports: Ports to REFUSE at the gateway: a client dialling the database or a management panel gets a broken connection through the same redirect as everything else, so nothing answers on the public network. The port must not appear in ingress_ports. Set allow_protected_ports: true (or delete the list) to leave these ports to their own listener.
_ui: Monitoring has three things that can be managed from the dashboard without touching gateway.json: label an unlisted address as checker/admin/team (tab 'Адреса'), route an extra public port (tab 'Сервисы', with auto-detection from the services' compose/.env files), and scan a directory. Labels persist to <data>/state/labels.json, services to <data>/state/services.json, and both are applied live and at boot.
